final:
One was PARTIALLY_VALID, so I narrowed its wording to the part that holds up.

### HIGH severity (1)
- **`flusher.py:254`: a hung flusher is never killed.** The PR wraps the kill in `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The flusher's processes come from the spawn context, and those are not `multiprocessing.Process` instances (I checked in the interpreter: the check returns `False`). So `kill()` never runs, which is a regression: the old code always killed. When a flusher hangs:
  - the old process keeps running;
  - a replacement starts on the same shards and writes to the same health and backpressure counters;
  - each restart leaks another process, and both processes may send the same segments to Kafka twice.

  The same check in `join()` means `terminate()` is also skipped on shutdown, but that part was already there before this PR.

### MEDIUM severity (2)
- **`flusher.py:93`: the flush limit gets bigger when there is more than one flusher process.** Each process has its own buffer, so `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` is divided by that process's shard count only. With N processes, each flush cycle can load about N times more segments, and flusher backpressure starts N times later. The default of 1 process is unaffected, and this may be intended, so the comment asks for it to be documented or for the global shard count to be passed in. This is the one the validator marked PARTIALLY_VALID.
- **`flusher.py:185`: shard metric tags have too many values and inconsistent keys.** The tag value is a comma-joined list of shards (e.g. `"0,1,...,63"` with the default of 1 process). Every rebalance produces a new value, which creates new metric series. `wait_produce` also uses the tag key `shards` while the other metrics use `shard`.

### LOW severity (3)
- **`flusher.py:300`: repeated Redis memory checks.** Every submit asks the whole Redis cluster for memory stats (`INFO`) once per process buffer, although all buffers use the same cluster. The result is still correct; it's just N redundant calls on the main thread.
- **`consumers/__init__.py:435`: `--flusher-processes` is not validated.** A negative value crashes with `KeyError` when partitions are assigned, and `0` quietly means one process per shard. The fix is `click.IntRange(min=1)`.
- **`test_consumer.py:62`: the new `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing.** The test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op earlier on, so the timing race it was meant to fix is still there.

### Dropped in validation (0)
- None.

I also noticed two dead-code items and left them out as not worth a comment: `_create_process_for_shard` is never called, and the `if not process: continue` check can never be true.

Files are in `bench/runs/getsentry_sentry-93824/pr-proof/`:
- `drafts_raw.json`: the drafts as written, before validation.
- `drafts.json`: `{"kept": [...], "dropped": [...]}`, with each validator's verdict and evidence attached.

There is no PR link because I didn't contact GitHub.
